# ai-memory Pi vendor patch

`../ai-memory-pi.ts` is intentionally a single-file vendor extension, not a repository-owned extension refactor. It is generated by pinned **ai-memory 2.1.0** plus `ai-memory-pi-native-mcp.patch`. Tests live in `../ai-memory-pi-tests/` so the canonical test runner can select them without adding a Pi entrypoint or changing manifests.

## Why retain a hook-only extension?

The [upstream Pi section](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/blob/v2.1.0/docs/mcp-install.md#pi) says Pi has no native MCP configuration; the same statement remained on upstream main when inspected. That describes an older Pi. Installed Pi 1.2.0 documents native `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` in its `docs/mcp.md`.

Native MCP replaces **only the tools bridge**, not ai-memory's lifecycle capture or automatic handoff context injection. The patch deletes the entire bridge and its startup invocation. There is no fallback, native-config parser, or custom `registerTool`. Missing, disabled, or broken native MCP is handled by Pi, not silently replaced by custom tools. The remaining upstream capture, capture exclusion policy, offline spool, auth-token resolution, handoff, managed-run, and compaction code is unchanged.

The only added behavior is stable `before_agent_start` guidance that native memory calls need explicit scope. Native MCP tool events still flow through Pi's existing `tool_call` / `tool_result` hooks. Names such as `mcp__ai_memory__memory_status` remain non-file/unknown to upstream capture policy, just as legacy `memory_status` was; they are captured normally. Hook HTTP requests are not Pi tool calls, so capture does not recurse.

## Scope and authentication

Native HTTP tools no longer receive the bridge's `X-Memory-Actor-Session-Id` / `Mcp-Session-Id` headers containing the current Pi session ID. Pi advertises MCP roots, but ai-memory 2.1.0 does not resolve tool scope from roots. Lifecycle `/hook` and `/handoff` requests retain their own session ID, cwd, marker routing parameters, managed-run ID, and authentication.

As documented in [ai-memory auto-scope](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/blob/v2.1.0/docs/auto-scope.md), static MCP clients **must pass both `workspace` and `project`** for project-scoped calls when concurrent sessions may exist. Use explicit `scopes` / `global` only for intentional cross-project queries. Pass `session_id` when targeting a particular session on tools supporting it. Do not invent a shared environment session ID or assume the server's latest active project belongs to this Pi session.

Native MCP authentication is configured separately in Pi's native server entry; it does not inherit the hook extension's token-file lookup. No credentials belong in this patch. Native transport setup and its explicit-scope instructions are managed by the repository installer.

## Regenerate and verify

Never run `install-hooks --agent pi --apply`: the deployed extension directory is a symlink into this repository.

From the repository root:

```sh
# Checks the installed binary's version, generates into a temporary directory,
# applies the exact patch without fuzz, and compares with the tracked extension.
python3 configs/agents/pi/extensions/vendor/refresh-ai-memory-pi.py

# Deliberately refresh after reviewing the pinned generator and patch:
python3 configs/agents/pi/extensions/vendor/refresh-ai-memory-pi.py --write

bun run test:pi-extensions ai-memory-pi-tests
bun run test:pi-extensions:e2e ai-memory-pi-tests
bun run lint:pi-extensions
bun run typecheck:pi-extensions
```

Use `--binary /path/to/ai-memory` to select the pinned binary. A version mismatch or patch drift fails rather than dropping lifecycle changes. Update the pin, patch, and tests together when upgrading upstream.

The default tests exercise real hook code through fake Pi with mocked external fetch. The spec runs real Pi RPC with the actual vendor module, a deterministic local model, isolated agent/data directories, and an external-service fetch fixture. It proves handoff injection and prompt capture without contacting or mutating the user's memory service. Native MCP transport connectivity is a separate integration boundary.
